title: The operator reads the design and knows which version the plan was built on
description:
SPIDR child 3 of task-8a6d6660c31c4e119f962d13e6f1505d (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). dependsOn child 1 (task-5e90317e80ac4b86a9704b6b8ba8874a, the aggregate and reads) and child 2 (task-de0598236f3b4d95aa3b6098b9d56995, the staffed step). PROOF ROW: it owns the e2e, the live drive and the docs, so neither sibling files its own evidence row (global rail 21).

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: a Design tab on the opened goal showing the five sections and the version; the operator read `/design/read` wired through the browser's exact-key decoder and proxy pin; the plan-approval card naming the design VERSION the plan was compiled against; and the request-changes path (a comment-driven resubmit bumps the version).

THE VERSION ON THE APPROVAL CARD IS THE POINT, not a label. The parent's design is that the human accepts the design IMPLICITLY by approving the plan - so the approval card must say WHICH design version that plan was compiled against, or the human is approving a plan against a design they may not have read. `apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/approve-plan-gate.tsx` (78 lines) and approve-plan.tsx are where it lands.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-20a6d1eb:
- approve-plan.tsx is 263 LINES, already over the 250-line ceiling this epic's rows carry. task-a988ca1c240347178c54348c470d07ed is planned to SPLIT it as its own step 2; if that row has not landed, this row must split before adding, or it ships a violation.
- The browser read clients in apps/control-room/src/live/ decode with EXACT-KEY record checks that refuse an unexpected key set; `/design/read` needs its decoder and its pin in dev-proxy-paths.ts (the sorted list at :6-37).
- The goal screen's tabs and the board live under apps/control-room/src/v2/.

CONCURRENT EDITORS on approve-plan.tsx / approve-plan-gate.tsx: task-a988ca1c (Reject on the plan gate) owns both. Coordinate rather than collide - it splits the file, this row adds one line of provenance to the card.
definitionOfDone: The opened goal shows a Design tab with the five sections and the version, read through `/design/read` with an EXACT-KEY decoder (a frame with an extra key is REFUSED, one missing a key is REFUSED) and its pin added to dev-proxy-paths.ts. Assert against a REAL daemon frame that a named entity from the data-model section reaches the rendered tab.

THE PLAN-APPROVAL CARD NAMES THE DESIGN VERSION the plan was compiled against. Assert the version string is rendered on the card, and assert the card still renders when the goal has NO design (the skip path from child 2) with words saying so rather than a blank or a zero - a human approving a plan built with no design must be told that, since approval is the implicit acceptance.
A resubmit bumps the version and the tab shows the newer one; assert the older version is still readable, since the operator's question is what CHANGED.
The skip path renders honestly: a goal planned without a design shows the Design tab stating the step was skipped, not an empty tab that reads as 'the design is blank'.

A Playwright journey against a REAL daemon covers a design being submitted by a scripted seat double and the operator reading it, with the `pnpm test:e2e:browser` count line quoted. Control-room fixtures are REAL daemon frames captured from that run.

LIVE DRIVE on UnAI or a fresh project: a REAL seat (not a double) submits a design - transcript and design ref in a row comment under ~4500 chars. If the seat cannot produce a valid design, record the DESIGN_SHAPE_INVALID refusal verbatim; that is a real finding about the mission, never worked around.

VISION and README journey step 4 ('UX and architecture') marked as running, with the date. Gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm test:e2e:browser`.
taskRails: THIS ROW PROVES, IT DOES NOT REBUILD. If the tab cannot render because the aggregate is missing a section, comment on child 1 and report_blocked; if the compiler mission lacks the design ref, that is child 2's.
approve-plan.tsx IS ALREADY OVER THE 250-LINE CEILING (263). Either task-a988ca1c has landed its split, or this row splits before adding. Measure with `wc -l` before writing, not at the final gate.
EXACT-KEY DECODER for /design/read, matching every sibling in apps/control-room/src/live/. A tolerant decoder defeats the mechanism that detects a stale daemon.
THE NO-DESIGN CASE IS RENDERED IN WORDS, never as an empty tab. A blank design tab reads as 'the design is empty', which is a different and false claim.
ASCII-only sources and apostrophe-free JSX text (scheduler package-boundary scan); check any new testid namespace is free; keep every production file under 250 lines.

THE EXACT-KEY DECODER IS GENUINELY EXACT, checked at source rather than taken from the commit subject. `live-design.ts` snapshots with `Reflect.ownKeys`, refuses when `keys.length !== expected.length` or any key is outside the expected set, and refuses any property whose descriptor is missing, non-enumerable, or accessor-backed (`!("value" in descriptor)`) — so a getter cannot smuggle a value past it, and arrays are length-checked as `ownKeys.length !== value.length + 1`. Extra key REFUSED and missing key REFUSED both hold by construction.

A DoD WORDING DISCREPANCY I AM FLAGGING RATHER THAN SILENTLY RESOLVING. DoD 1 and the description say "the five sections". The decoder's roster at `live-design.ts:30` names SIX: `apiSurface, componentList, dataModel, nonFunctional, openDecisions, screens`. implementationPlan.note:
THE PLAN FOLD NOW NAMES THE DESIGN VERSION IT WAS COMPILED AGAINST (DoD 2). `approve-plan.tsx` untouched, as instructed.

NEW `apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/design-version-note.tsx`, 107 lines (cap 250). Reads through the SIBLING `readDesign` from `live/live-design.js` — the same `/design/read` and the same exact-key decoder the Design tab uses — with an injectable `read` for tests, mirroring `LiveDesign`'s read-on-mount and stale-subject guard so an old goal cannot publish a late answer. Renders `data-testid="cr.approve.design-version"` in every state. Apostrophe-free throughout.

FOUR STATES, and the two that matter are the ones a blank would collapse.
- DESIGN present: `Design version 2. Approving this plan accepts that design.` The number is the operator's anchor, so it is in the words, not a title attribute.
- `DESIGN_REVISION_ABSENT @ LEDGER`: `This plan was compiled with no design. Approving it accepts the plan alone.` NEVER a blank, never a zero — the DoD's point is that a human approving a plan built with no design must be TOLD, because approval is the implicit acceptance.
- Sibling SKIP status (child 2's path): `The design step was skipped, so this plan was compiled with no design.` plus the recorded reason.
- ANY OTHER refusal: `OutcomeNote` carrying CODE and LAYER. This is the distinction I was most careful about — a read failure is not a fact about the plan, so it must not read as "no design". The test asserts that negatively.

WHY IT READS TWICE RATHER THAN SHARING THE TAB'S FETCH, written at the site: sharing one read would couple the approval surface to whether the operator had opened the Design tab. Same endpoint and same decoder means the version named here and the version on the tab cannot drift.

DoD 3, NO VERSION PICKER — stated in the file so nobody adds one later. An older revision stays readable by asking the daemon for it (`/design/read` accepts a version), which step 3's journey exercises; a picker here would be a second way to name a revision and a second thing to keep in step with the tab.

MOUNT, ADD-ONLY. `cordum-app.tsx` 482 -> 490 lines: one import plus the element rendered immediately after `<ApprovePlan … />`, INSIDE the plan fold `<details>`, with a comment saying why position is the argument — a version note outside the fold would not be part of the approval the human is giving. A test asserts the ORDER (`indexOf(ApprovePlan) < indexOf(LiveDesignVersionNote) < indexOf(</details>)`), not mere presence, so a later move out of the fold reds.

That is the human-gate fence holding.

THE MID-FLIGHT CHANGE. Between my green run at 19:11Z and my next run, commit `4ac0dbda fix: harden release and deployment review gaps` (owner, no Moe-Task trailer) REWROTE the two files this row's DoD 2 lands on: `LiveDesignVersionNote` now takes `planningRunRef` and calls `readDesign(headers, goalRef, undefined, planningRunRef)`, and cordum-app.tsx:350 passes `planningRunRef={planRunId}`. The daemon then reads `readCompiledContractBinding` (design-store.ts:197-202) and answers DESIGN_RECORD_MALFORMED when the run has no compiled design binding. My journey went red with `Received string: "The design version behind this plan could not be read right now.DetailsDESIGN_RECORD_MALFORMED @ LEDGER"` at the DoD 2 assertion.

I FOLLOWED THE NEW PRODUCTION SEMANTICS RATHER THAN REVERTING IT, because it is strictly closer to what DoD 2 asks: the fold now names the version THIS PLAN RUN WAS COMPILED AGAINST (`compile-dispatcher.ts:292` records `designVersion: design.ok ? design.record.version : null`), not the goal's newest revision. The journey now: design v1 -> tab Version 1 + ShelfItemV1Marker -> design v2 (resubmit) -> tab Version 2 + ShelfItemV2Marker -> `/design/read {goalRef, version:1}` still answers version 1 with ITS entity and not v2's -> a scripted seat compiles the plan (`planning.submit_decomposition`, node scopes copied from plan-reject-replan.spec.ts) -> fold says "Design version 2" and NOT "Design version 1".

THE ORDER IS FORCED, and I only learned it by measuring: once a decomposition compiles, the goal has left the design rung and the surface offers approval.decide/decide_intent instead of design.submit, so a resubmit attempted after the compile dies with `no design.submit offer among approval.decide@run-..., ...`. Comment in the spec says so at the step.

1. `versionWords` "Design version" -> "Design revision": e2e RED with `Expected substring: "Design version 1"` / `Received: "Design revision 1. ..."` at the fold assertion. Restore sha 95FBEB10EC4C5628...
2. Drop the planning-run selector (`read(goalRef, "")`): the new unit arm goes RED, `expected [ { goalRef: 'goal-1', ...} ] to deeply equal [...]`, 1 failed | 13 passed. Restore sha 0075BE786003C76C...
Drill 2 exists because the e2e CANNOT distinguish this: with v2 latest at compile time, a note that ignored the binding and read the latest would still print "Design version 2". The unit arm asserts the selector reaches the reader (`seen toEqual [{goalRef:"goal-1", planningRunRef:"run-7"}]`). That is stated so nobody reads the e2e as proving more than it does.
